text: Each of the counsellors will think of his own interests, and the prince will not know how to control them or to see through them. And they are not to be found otherwise, because men will always prove untrue to you unless they are kept honest by constraint. Therefore it must be inferred that good counsels, whencesoever they come, are born of the wisdom of the prince, and not the wisdom of the prince from good counsels.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXIII, How flatterers should be avoided
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
